By default, the unbiased 29| * "sample variance" definitional formula is used: 30| *

31| * variance = sum((x_i - mean)^2) / (n - 1)

32| *

33| * where mean is the {@link Mean} and n is the number 34| * of sample observations.

35| *

36| * The definitional formula does not have good numerical properties, so 37| * this implementation does not compute the statistic using the definitional 38| * formula.

    39| *
  • The getResult method computes the variance using 40| * updating formulas based on West's algorithm, as described in 41| * Chan, T. F. and 42| * J. G. Lewis 1979, Communications of the ACM, 43| * vol. 22 no. 9, pp. 526-531.
    • 44| *
  • The evaluate methods leverage the fact that they have the 45| * full array of values in memory to execute a two-pass algorithm. 46| * Specifically, these methods use the "corrected two-pass algorithm" from 47| * Chan, Golub, Levesque, Algorithms for Computing the Sample Variance, 48| * American Statistician, vol. 37, no. 3 (1983) pp. 242-247.
49| * Note that adding values using increment or 50| * incrementAll and then executing getResult will 51| * sometimes give a different, less accurate, result than executing 52| * evaluate with the full array of values. The former approach 53| * should only be used when the full array of values is not available.

54| *

55| * The "population variance" ( sum((x_i - mean)^2) / n ) can also 56| * be computed using this statistic. The isBiasCorrected 57| * property determines whether the "population" or "sample" value is 58| * returned by the evaluate and getResult methods. 59| * To compute population variances, set this property to false. 60| *

61| *

62| * Note that this implementation is not synchronized. If 63| * multiple threads access an instance of this class concurrently, and at least 64| * one of the threads invokes the increment() or 65| * clear() method, it must be synchronized externally.

66| * 67| * @version $Id$ 68| */ 69| public class Variance extends AbstractStorelessUnivariateStatistic implements Serializable, WeightedEvaluation { 70| 71| /** Serializable version identifier */ 72| private static final long serialVersionUID = -9111962718267217978L; 73| 74| /** SecondMoment is used in incremental calculation of Variance*/ 75| protected SecondMoment moment = null; 76| 77| /** 78| * Whether or not {@link #increment(double)} should increment 79| * the internal second moment. When a Variance is constructed with an 80| * external SecondMoment as a constructor parameter, this property is 81| * set to false and increments must be applied to the second moment 82| * directly. 83| */ 84| protected boolean incMoment = true; 85| 86| /** 87| * Whether or not bias correction is applied when computing the 88| * value of the statistic. True means that bias is corrected. See 89| * {@link Variance} for details on the formula. 90| */ 91| private boolean isBiasCorrected = true; 92| 93| /** 94| * Constructs a Variance with default (true) isBiasCorrected 95| * property. 96| */ 97| public Variance() { 98| moment = new SecondMoment(); 99| } 100| 101| /** 102| * Constructs a Variance based on an external second moment. 103| * When this constructor is used, the statistic may only be 104| * incremented via the moment, i.e., {@link #increment(double)} 105| * does nothing; whereas {@code m2.increment(value)} increments 106| * both {@code m2} and the Variance instance constructed from it. 107| * 108| * @param m2 the SecondMoment (Third or Fourth moments work 109| * here as well.) 110| */ 111| public Variance(final SecondMoment m2) { 112| incMoment = false; 113| this.moment = m2; 114| } 115| 116| /** 117| * Constructs a Variance with the specified isBiasCorrected 118| * property 119| * 120| * @param isBiasCorrected setting for bias correction - true means 121| * bias will be corrected and is equivalent to using the argumentless 122| * constructor 123| */ 124| public Variance(boolean isBiasCorrected) { 125| moment = new SecondMoment(); 126| this.isBiasCorrected = isBiasCorrected; 127| } 128| 129| /** 130| * Constructs a Variance with the specified isBiasCorrected 131| * property and the supplied external second moment. 132| * 133| * @param isBiasCorrected setting for bias correction - true means 134| * bias will be corrected 135| * @param m2 the SecondMoment (Third or Fourth moments work 136| * here as well.) 137| */ 138| public Variance(boolean isBiasCorrected, SecondMoment m2) { 139| incMoment = false; 140| this.moment = m2; 141| this.isBiasCorrected = isBiasCorrected; 142| } 143| 144| /** 145| * Copy constructor, creates a new {@code Variance} identical 146| * to the {@code original} 147| * 148| * @param original the {@code Variance} instance to copy 149| */ 150| public Variance(Variance original) { 151| copy(original, this); 152| } 153| 154| /** 155| * {@inheritDoc} 156| *

If all values are available, it is more accurate to use 157| * {@link #evaluate(double[])} rather than adding values one at a time 158| * using this method and then executing {@link #getResult}, since 159| * evaluate leverages the fact that is has the full 160| * list of values together to execute a two-pass algorithm. 161| * See {@link Variance}.

162| * 163| *

Note also that when {@link #Variance(SecondMoment)} is used to 164| * create a Variance, this method does nothing. In that case, the 165| * SecondMoment should be incremented directly.

166| */ 167| @Override 168| public void increment(final double d) { 169| if (incMoment) { 170| moment.increment(d); 171| } 172| } 173| 174| /** 175| * {@inheritDoc} 176| */ 177| @Override 178| public double getResult() { 179| if (moment.n == 0) { 180| return Double.NaN; 181| } else if (moment.n == 1) { 182| return 0d; 183| } else { 184| if (isBiasCorrected) { 185| return moment.m2 / (moment.n - 1d); 186| } else { 187| return moment.m2 / (moment.n); 188| } 189| } 190| } 191| 192| /** 193| * {@inheritDoc} 194| */ 195| public long getN() { 196| return moment.getN(); 197| } 198| 199| /** 200| * {@inheritDoc} 201| */
